key_insight: MetaRigor makes automated meta-analysis more verifiable by preserving result identity and separating context-dependent scientific interpretation from programmable rules and checks.
engineering_relevance: Research-agent pipelines should track study, comparison, population, outcome, time point, and analysis conditions explicitly to prevent local errors from propagating into final reports.
method: Organize results as Study × Target units with explicit identity and source binding.
Use Task Contracts to define scientific decision boundaries at each workflow stage.
Assign contextual interpretation to LLMs and formal rules, computation, validation, and source verification to programs.
evidence_signal: Across five evaluated stages, MetaRigor achieved 86.29% complete-result delivery F1 and 80.20% domain-level certainty agreement; seven end-to-end cases yielded 77.01% aggregate F1, 9.78 percentage points above the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The seven-case end-to-end evaluation provides limited evidence of generalizability; explicit contracts and provenance checks still require validation for new review settings.
paper_title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
